article_title: Teaching Aids a Special Pedagogy Tool of Brain Development in School Children, Interest and Academic Achievement to Enhance Future Technology
citation: Joseph, O. C. (2015). Teaching Aids a Special Pedagogy Tool of Brain Development in School Children, Interest and Academic Achievement to Enhance Future Technology. Journal of Education and Practice, 6(29). https://www.iiste.org
title: Interest Inventory Test (IIT) and Academic Achievement Test (AAT) instruments
description: The researcher designed two ten-item instruments: the "Inte rest Inventory Test (IIT) to measure the children i nterest" and the "Academic Achievement Test (AAT) to measure the chil dren academic achievement level". Both were validated by three professors from three universities and pilot tested with fifty children outside the study population. Reliability was 0.71 for the IIT (Cronbach Alpha) and 0.79 for the AAT (Kuder-Richardson formula 20).
requirements: Administration with the assistance of class teachers, pre-tested before teaching and post-tested after
constraints: Reliability values of 0.71 and 0.79 were obtained from a pilot with fifty children not part of the study population
examples: Both instruments were administered as pre-tests and post-tests to the 400 pupils across the ten schools
key_sources: Joseph, O. C. (2015). Teaching Aids a Special Pedagogy Tool of Brain Development in School Children, Interest and Academic Achievement to Enhance Future Technology. Journal of Education and Practice, 6(29). https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1081258

article_title: Autograder+: A Multi-Faceted AI Framework for Rich Pedagogical Feedback in Programming Education
citation: Vikrant Sahu, Dr. Gagan Raj Gupta, Raghav Borikar, and Nitin Mane. 2025. Autograder+: A Multi-Faceted AI Framework for Rich Pedagogical Feedback in Programming Education. CODS '25. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26402
title: IITBh PC25 evaluation dataset of 600 TA-annotated student submissions
description: IITBh PC25 is the article's primary validation corpus: 600 student submissions collected from internal programming courses at IIT Bhilai, spanning 20 LeetCode-style algorithmic problems such as Fibonacci and Disarium. The article notes it "contains a diverse range of correct solutions, partially correct attempts, and common logical and syntax errors." Each submission was manually evaluated by Teaching Assistants who provided "gold-standard" pedagogical feedback, and these (submission, TA_Feedback) pairs serve as the reference ground truth for SBERT and BERTScore-based evaluation of the feedback models.
requirements: Manual TA annotation of each submission with pedagogical feedback to serve as reference ground truth
constraints: Limited to 20 LeetCode-style algorithmic problems from a single institution's internal programming courses
target_learners: university students in internal programming courses at IIT Bhilai
examples: The dataset table (Table 2) lists IITBh PC25 as 600 submissions from an internal programming course used for evaluation, alongside the 171,000-example NVidia ORC external corpus and 1,000 IITBh PW25S workshop submissions.
key_sources: Vikrant Sahu, Dr. Gagan Raj Gupta, Raghav Borikar, and Nitin Mane. 2025. Autograder+: A Multi-Faceted AI Framework for Rich Pedagogical Feedback in Programming Education. CODS '25. https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26402

article_title: Formative experience for intensive instruction physics courses: Evaluation and results in an Electromagnetism course
citation: Marcela Vallejo, Ema Huerta, Joselen M. Peña, José Leiva, Ethan Rodriguez. (2026). Formative experience for intensive instruction physics courses: Evaluation and results in an Electromagnetism course. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12404
title: Integrated pedagogical proposal for an electromagnetism IIC combining six active strategies with formative assessment
description: The article designed a training proposal for a three-week, 45-hour intensive electromagnetism course, built from a teacher focus group and literature review. It states the proposal "included some of the active methodological strategies described in sections I B and I C, among which the following were selected: interactive lectures, direct teaching, collaborative work, problem-based learning, use of online simulation tools, and formative assessment." The EG followed this proposal while the CG received non-innovated lessons, and an activity log for the 2024 summer course appears in the appendix.
requirements: Teachers with previous experience teaching the subject in a regular semester, able to regulate pace from less to more difficult content
constraints: Designed for a three-week remedial IIC with exclusive student dedication and small cohorts of about 20 students
target_learners: Undergraduate STEM students re-enrolling in a failed high-failure-rate course in an intensive format
target_learning_goals: Conceptual understanding of electromagnetism (electrostatics, direct current circuits, magnetostatics, electromagnetic induction)
examples: The 2024 intensive summer course on electromagnetism, whose activity log is shown in the appendix, implemented the proposal with two 90-minute blocks per day subdivided into two 40-minute sessions.
key_sources: Marcela Vallejo, Ema Huerta, Joselen M. Peña, José Leiva, Ethan Rodriguez. (2026). Formative experience for intensive instruction physics courses: Evaluation and results in an Electromagnetism course. https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12404
